thread.title: Apple Earnings: Shares Gain 3% in After Hours

author: Jon Swartz
title: Apple Earnings: Shares Gain 3% in After Hours
text:
By Jon Swartz July 31, 2018 5:58 p.m. ET Apple shares climbed 3% in after-hours trading Tuesday after it reported a spike in earnings and revenue that were in line with analyst estimates.
The company earned $2.34 per share on revenue of $53.3 billion for its fiscal third quarter, compared with EPS of $1.67 and revenue of $45.4 billion.
Analysts on average expected Apple (AAPL) to post earnings of $2.16 per share, according to FactSet . They expected revenue of $52.34 billion. In February, Apple said it expected revenue of between $51.5 billion and $53.5 billion for the quarter.
The Cupertino, Calif.-based company benefited from a 31% surge in Apple's booming Services division–it includes Apple Pay , iCloud , and Apple Music –and continued growth for iPhone and China . Services reached a record $9.55 billion, and is well on the way to a runrate of $14 billion per quarter by 2020, the company said.
Even though iPhone unit shipments inched up 1% to 41.3 million, revenue catapulted 20% to $29.9 billion because the $999 iPhone X was the top-selling brand, Apple CEO Tim Cook said in a conference call with analysts today. This resulted in the average selling price of iPhone reached $724, a sizable bump from a year ago.
The iPhone revenue allayed fears among some investors after Samsung Electronics (South Korea: 005930) registered its slowest quarterly profit growth in more than a year Tuesday because its Galaxy S9 smartphone missed sales targets. Samsung's performance underscored mounting concerns that Apple, too, would be victimized by a saturated smartphone market.
Sales rose 19% during the quarter, to $9.55 billion, in Greater China, where Apple gleans about 20% of its revenue. It remains to be seen what will happen in future quarters in China, which is locked with the U.S. in an escalating trade war. In the conference call, Cook said he was optimistic the issue would be smoothed over.
Apple's guidance was also encouraging. It said fourth-quarter revenue, which will include initial sales of what should be three new iPhone models to be announced in September, will be between $60 billion and $62 billion, besting Wall Street predictions of $59.47 billion, according to StreetAccount .
The trajectory puts Apple well on its inevitable path to becoming the first $1 trillion company in market value this year.
"Apple will be the first company in history to reach this milestone, but others will quickly follow, notably Amazon.com, then Alphabet, which I forecast will arrive before Microsoft," predicts Ken Berman at Gorilla Trades .
Investors were watching closely to see if Apple would be entangled in the FAANG meltdown, which hammered shares of Facebook (FB) and Netflix (NFLX) last week in a broader sell-off. Amazon (AMZN) and Alphabet (GOOGL) fared much better after each reported quarterly earnings.
About the only impediments holding Apple from $1 trillion are buybacks and dividends, which enhance the company's share price though doesn't necessarily enhance its overall market value. Those shares repurchased are no longer in circulation, and can no longer be invested in future projects.
In its fiscal third quarter, Apple declared a cash dividend of 73 cents per share and repurchased about $20 billion in common stock. With approximately 4.9 billion shares, it will take the stock price of about $204 for Apple to reach $1 trillion.
